title: Add simulated tool-assertion harness and guided authoring tutorial for safe tool-calls
author: Leah Cheng
release_notes: Add a small, reusable harness for simulating tool-calls in RAG/agent quickstarts; ship a guided authoring doc and two example quickstarts demonstrating deterministic safety assertions for tool interactions.
body: Summary: Introduces a lightweight 'tool-assertion' harness and a guided authoring tutorial to make it easy for developers to write deterministic, testable tool-calling examples for RAG/agent quickstarts. Motivation: Agent and tool-calling examples frequently rely on external services or nondeterministic behavior which makes local debugging and CI validation brittle. This PR provides a simulation harness that lets examples assert tool-call safety (argument shapes, allowed endpoints, response contracts) without requiring a full service. It also adds an authoring doc that walks through converting an existing agent example to use the harness and adding unit-style assertions. | What this changes: 1) examples/rag/tool-assertion-harness/: a small Python and TypeScript harness with adapter stubs and assertion helpers; 2) docs/authoring/tool-call-safety.md: step-by-step tutorial describing the mental model, recommended assertions, and CI integration patterns; 3) examples/rag/quickstarts/safe-webhook-demo/: two minimal quickstarts (one Node, one Python) that demonstrate common patterns (webhook proxy, long-poll simulation) using the harness; 4) tests/integration/tool_assertion_smoke.py and examples/ts/test/tool_assertion.spec.ts: CI smoke tests that run the harness in-headless mode. | Design details: - Harness core: lightweight in-process simulator that exposes a configurable set of endpoints (synchronous and async mock responses), an 'expect_call' API to declare required tool-call signatures, and a short DSL for response fixtures. - Authoring doc: emphasises three guardrails—(a) assert argument schema rather than exact strings, (b) pin simulated latencies to test timeouts, (c) use replay fixtures for deterministic generation steps. - CI integration: add a matrix job that runs both quickstarts against the harness and fails on assertion violation. The harness intentionally requires only the standard test runtime (pytest / jest) and no external network. | Backwards compatibility: all changes are additive to examples and docs. No runtime code in the serving runtime or SDKs was modified. Migration notes: Maintainers can adopt the harness by replacing direct external tool calls with the harness adapter shim; the authoring doc includes a checklist and a small codemod snippet. | Checklist: - [x] Implementation of harness (Python + TS) - [x] Authoring doc and short checklist - [x] Two converted quickstarts and example usage - [x] CI job and smoke tests - [x] Local README + troubleshooting section - [x] Reviewer feedback addressed (see review threads) | Security & privacy: The harness never transmits data off-host; simulated fixtures are stored under examples/ and are marked as synthetic. The doc calls out how to sanitize real PII before creating fixtures. | Why this is valuable: Reduces flakiness in quickstart examples and makes it straightforward for engineers to add deterministic checks around tool-calling behavior, improving confidence in example-driven onboarding and preventing regressions in agent integrations.

review_threads: Oliver Park (reviewer): Can we keep the harness surface tiny so it doesn't become another dependency? Response (Leah): Yes—kept to two files per language and documented the minimal public API. Ravi Menon: Please add an example that asserts the KV-cache prefix is forwarded to the tool caller when present. Response: Added a small fixture and test in the Python quickstart to demonstrate the KV prefix case. Anisa Kaur: Linting + TS build failed on first run. Response: Fixed type declarations and added a small mock helper to the TS harness; reran CI and it passed. Final: all reviewers approved and requested the small portability note added to the doc.
ci_checks: CI matrix: linux-py37 (pytest) — pass; linux-node14 (jest) — pass; linters — pass; docs-linkcheck — pass; smoke-retry (flaky test re-run) — pass. Coverage: examples smoke tests exercise ~85% of harness code paths. One advisory: jest snapshot updated intentionally.
merge: Merged by squash on 2026-02-24 (merge method: squash). Commit message preserved main points from PR body and credited author. Release: flagged for inclusion in next docs release (changelog entry prepared).
notes_for_maintainers: How to adopt: 1) copy harness adapter from examples/rag/tool-assertion-harness to your example repo; 2) add expectation calls around tool invocation sites (see examples); 3) run smoke CI job locally via ./scripts/run-harness-smoke.sh. Troubleshooting: common failure is schema mismatch—use the provided schema-assert helper to get readable diffs.
human_readable_summary: Adds a tiny simulation harness and a docs tutorial to make tool-calling examples deterministic and testable. Two quickstarts updated to demonstrate the pattern. CI smoke tests now run harness assertions to reduce flakiness in examples and docs demonstrations.
